title: Is This Your Bag?

story.text: This is a **classroom**. It's a **lovely** **day** **today**.
This is Mr Adel. **Mr** Adel is a **teacher**. This is Saad, **and** this is Fahad. Saad and Fahad are **students**. Saad and Fahad are **classmates**.

story.speaker: Mr Adel
story.text: **Good morning**, **class**! **Welcome**!

story.speaker: Saad and Fahad
story.text: Good morning, Mr Adel.

story.speaker: Mr Adel
story.text: **Sit down**, **please**.
Saad is at a **table** **with** Fahad.

story.speaker: Saad
story.text: **Hello**! **My** **name** is Saad. **What**'s **your** name?

story.speaker: Fahad
story.text: My name is Fahad. **Nice to meet you**.

story.speaker: Saad
story.text: Nice to meet you, Fahad. **How are you?**

story.speaker: Fahad
story.text: I'm **fine**, **thanks**. And you?

story.speaker: Saad
story.text: I'm **OK**. I'm **hungry**!
Mr Adel is at the **board**.

story.speaker: Mr Adel
story.text: OK, class. This is an **English** **book**. And **what's this**?

story.speaker: Saad
story.text: It's a **pen**.

story.speaker: Mr Adel
story.text: **Yes**! And this?

story.speaker: Fahad
story.text: It's a **notebook**.

story.speaker: Mr Adel
story.text: And what's this?

story.speaker: Saad
story.text: It's a **computer**.

story.speaker: Mr Adel
story.text: **No**, Saad. It's a **television**!

story.speaker: Saad
story.text: Oh! A television!

story.speaker: Mr Adel
story.text: **Thank you**, class. **Goodbye**! **See you later!**
Saad and Fahad are at the table. This is a bag, and this is a bag.

story.speaker: Saad
story.text: Fahad, is this your **bag**?

story.speaker: Fahad
story.text: My bag? What's this? It's a **sandwich**. And this is a **cake**. And this is a **bottle** of **water**.

story.speaker: Saad
story.text: Yes! It's my bag. My sandwich, my cake and my water!

story.speaker: Fahad
story.text: And this is my bag. What's this? It's a **phone**. This is a **key**. And this is an **ID card**.

story.speaker: Saad
story.text: What's the **first name**?

story.speaker: Fahad
story.text: The first name is Fahad. The **surname** is Al-Qahtani. Yes, it's my bag!

story.speaker: Saad
story.text: A sandwich, Fahad?

story.speaker: Fahad
story.text: Yes, please! I'm hungry and **thirsty**!

story.speaker: Saad
story.text: And a bottle of water?

story.speaker: Fahad
story.text: Thank you, Saad!
Saad and Fahad are at the table with a sandwich, a cake and a bottle of water. It's a lovely day!

story.speaker: Saad
story.text: **Have a nice day**, Fahad!

story.speaker: Fahad
story.text: Thanks, Saad. See you later!

title: A Photo at the Tower
setting: Tourists at a famous tower in Riyadh

story.text: This is Omar. **He** is **from** Riyadh. Riyadh is the **capital** **city** of **Saudi** Arabia. Omar is an **engineer**.
Today, Omar is at a **famous** **tower** in Riyadh. It's a **beautiful**, **tall** **building**. The **weather** is **fantastic**. It's **windy**, and the **sun** is beautiful.
Two **tourists** are at the tower, **too**. **They** are **on holiday**.

story.speaker: Marco
story.text: Hello! A **photo**, please?

story.speaker: Omar
story.text: Yes, OK. **Where** are you from?

story.speaker: Marco
story.text: I'm from **Italy**. My name is Marco. And this is Ken. He's from **Japan**.

story.speaker: Omar
story.text: Nice to meet you. Welcome to Saudi Arabia!

story.speaker: Ken
story.text: Thank you!

story.speaker: Omar
story.text: **How old** are you, Ken?

story.speaker: Ken
story.text: I'm **nineteen**. I'm a **teenager**! I'm a student.

story.speaker: Ken
story.text: And Marco is **thirty**. He's **married**. He's a **doctor**. **His** **hospital** is in Rome.

story.speaker: Omar
story.text: Rome? Is it the capital of Italy?

story.speaker: Marco
story.text: Yes, it is. It's a beautiful city, too.

story.speaker: Ken
story.text: And this is my **umbrella**. In Japan, the weather is **rainy**!

story.speaker: Omar
story.text: In Riyadh, an umbrella is for the sun!

story.speaker: Marco
story.text: This is my camera. Thank you, Omar!

story.speaker: Omar
story.text: OK. **Look at** the camera, please. One, two, three!

story.speaker: Ken
story.text: Look at the photo! Oh no! It's **awful**! Where's the tower?
The tower is tall. In the photo: Marco and Ken. The tower? No tower!

story.speaker: Omar
story.text: Ha! OK. Sit down, please. Marco, sit down. Ken, sit down. Look at the camera. One, two, three!

story.speaker: Marco
story.text: Look at the photo! Marco, Ken and the tower!

story.speaker: Ken
story.text: Fantastic! It's a beautiful photo!

story.speaker: Marco
story.text: Omar, where's the **market**? And where's the **mall**?

story.speaker: Omar
story.text: The mall is in the tower!

story.speaker: Ken
story.text: In the tower? Fantastic!

story.speaker: Omar
story.text: And the market? Look at the **map**. This is the tower, and this is the market. And this is a famous **mosque**.

story.speaker: Marco
story.text: Thank you, Omar. Riyadh is a fantastic city!

story.speaker: Omar
story.text: Goodbye! Have a nice day!

title: The Charity Walk

story.text: This is Khalid. He is a **nurse** at a hospital in Abha. This is his **brother**, Faisal. Faisal is a **boy**. He's twelve.

Today is a **charity** walk for the hospital. It's a walk in the hills of Abha. Khalid and Faisal are **excited**. **All** the people are excited. Khalid and Faisal are at the hill with a **backpack** and two bottles of water.
A woman is at a table with a **form**.

story.speaker: Woman
story.text: **Hi**! Your **full name**, please?

story.speaker: Khalid
story.text: Khalid Al-Ghamdi.

story.speaker: Woman
story.text: Your **nationality**?

story.speaker: Khalid
story.text: Saudi.

story.speaker: Woman
story.text: And your **mobile** number?

story.speaker: Khalid
story.text: **Wait a minute** … It's 055 123 4567.

story.speaker: Woman
story.text: And your **address**?

story.speaker: Faisal
story.text: **Sorry**? **I don't understand**.

story.speaker: Khalid
story.text: Your house, Faisal. Number 12, Al-Nahda Street.

story.speaker: Woman
story.text: **Thanks a lot**. **You're** number **forty** and forty-one. **Good luck**!

story.speaker: Woman
story.text: Is your brother a nurse, too?

story.speaker: Khalid
story.text: No, he isn't. He's a student.

story.speaker: Woman
story.text: Are you **ready**?

story.speaker: Faisal
story.text: Yes! We're ready!

story.speaker: Khalid
story.text: **Let's go**, Faisal!
The walk is **difficult**. Faisal is **tired** and thirsty. His bottle is **empty**.

story.speaker: Faisal
story.text: Khalid, I'm tired. Is it **far**?

story.speaker: Khalid
story.text: No, it isn't far. **Don't worry**.
This is a **guard**. He is **kind**.

story.speaker: Guard
story.text: **Excuse me**. **Can I help you?**

story.speaker: Khalid
story.text: **Yes, please**. My brother is thirsty.

story.speaker: Guard
story.text: Water? **Here you are**.

story.speaker: Faisal
story.text: Thanks a lot! You're **very** kind.

story.speaker: Khalid
story.text: Are you OK, Faisal?

story.speaker: Faisal
story.text: Yes, I'm OK **now**. I'm **strong**!
Now Khalid and Faisal aren't tired. They're **happy**.

story.speaker: Faisal
story.text: **Great!** We're **here**!

story.speaker: Woman
story.text: **Well done**! **Congratulations**!

story.speaker: Faisal
story.text: The walk isn't **boring**. It's **interesting**!

story.speaker: Khalid
story.text: And it's **important** for the hospital.

story.speaker: Woman
story.text: Faisal, how old are you?

story.speaker: Faisal
story.text: I'm twelve.

story.speaker: Woman
story.text: Twelve? You're very **brave**!

story.speaker: Faisal
story.text: Yes, I'm brave! And I'm not tired now. I'm happy, Khalid.

story.speaker: Khalid
story.text: **Me too**! Faisal, you're a great brother.

story.speaker: Faisal
story.text: And you're a great nurse!

title: The Big Match
setting: A football match at the stadium

story.text: Yousef and Bandar are **best friends**. They are from the same **village** in the **north** of Saudi Arabia. Now they are in Riyadh. Yousef is a **manager** at a **bank**. Bandar is an engineer at a big **company**.
Yousef and Bandar **have** a **hobby**. It's **football**! **Their** **team** is Al-Hilal.
Today is a big **match** at the **stadium**. It's in the **evening**. Yousef is at the stadium with **a lot of** **fans**. Where is Bandar? Bandar is **late**!
Yousef has a phone. It's a **call** to Bandar's **home**.

story.speaker: Bandar's mother
story.text: Hello?

story.speaker: Yousef
story.text: Hello. **Can I speak to** Bandar, please?

story.speaker: Bandar's mother
story.text: **Of course**. **Hold on** … Oh, sorry. Bandar isn't at home. He's at the **office**.

story.speaker: Yousef
story.text: At the office? The match is now!

story.speaker: Bandar's mother
story.text: Yes. His manager is with **him**.

story.speaker: Yousef
story.text: OK. Thank you.
It's a **message** from Bandar: "Sorry! I'm late. I'm **near** the stadium now."
And now Bandar is here! He has two burgers and two bottles of water.

story.speaker: Bandar
story.text: Sorry, Yousef! A burger for you.

story.speaker: Yousef
story.text: Thanks! I'm hungry. I **like** burgers!

story.speaker: Bandar
story.text: And I **want** a **goal**!
The match is fantastic. The **players** are **really** **good**. Salem is a **new** player. He is young and **clever**.
Salem has the **ball** … It's a goal! Al-Hilal: one. Al-Nassr: zero.
Yousef and Bandar are happy. All the fans are happy. The **coach** is happy, too.

story.speaker: Bandar
story.text: **Our** team is the winner!

story.speaker: Yousef
story.text: Yes! A really good match. And we're **together**!

story.speaker: Bandar
story.text: Sorry, I'm late, Yousef.

story.speaker: Yousef
story.text: That's OK. You're here, and you have burgers!
Bandar is a **funny** friend. He has his phone.

story.speaker: Bandar
story.text: Yousef, **give** **me** a **smile**! A photo, please!
In the photo: two best friends and a lot of happy fans.

title: The Arabic Menu

story.text: My name is Nasser. I'm Saudi, and I'm a **waiter**. I work at a small **restaurant** in Jeddah. We **love** **food** here, and our restaurant is very **popular**.

People from a lot of countries **eat** at our restaurant. I **speak** **Arabic** and English. I speak **a little** **Urdu**, too. Our chef, Imran, is **Pakistani**. He is a very good chef, and he is my friend.
Today, a man and a woman **come** to the restaurant. They are tourists. They are **British**.

story.speaker: Man
story.text: Hello! The **menu**, please.
I give them the menu. They look at it. But the menu is in Arabic!

story.speaker: Woman
story.text: Oh no! We **don't** speak Arabic. I don't understand.

story.speaker: Nasser
story.text: Don't worry. I speak English. This is **kabsa**. It's **rice** with **chicken** or **meat**. It's **delicious**!

story.speaker: Woman
story.text: Is it **spicy**?

story.speaker: Nasser
story.text: A little.

story.speaker: Woman
story.text: I don't like spicy food.

story.speaker: Nasser
story.text: **Do you like** **fish**?

story.speaker: Woman
story.text: Yes, I do! I love fish.

story.speaker: Man
story.text: I like chicken. And I like spicy food!
They **order** fish and rice for the woman, chicken kabsa for the man and two **orange** juices.

story.speaker: Man
story.text: Excuse me. A **fork** and a **spoon**, please.

story.speaker: Nasser
story.text: Here you are.
They eat, and they **enjoy** the food.

story.speaker: Nasser
story.text: Do you like the food?

story.speaker: Man
story.text: Yes, I do! The kabsa is **the best**!

story.speaker: Woman
story.text: The fish is delicious. I'm **full**!

story.speaker: Nasser
story.text: And **dessert**? We have **dates** and **chocolate** cake.

story.speaker: Man
story.text: Dates, please!

story.speaker: Man
story.text: The **bill**, please. **How much** is it?

story.speaker: Nasser
story.text: It's **ninety**-five **riyals**.

story.speaker: Man
story.text: Here you are. One hundred riyals, **cash**.

story.speaker: Nasser
story.text: Thank you. And this is your **change**: five riyals.
They smile.

story.speaker: Woman
story.text: Thank you, Nasser. You're very kind!
I love my job. I enjoy **languages**, and I love food!

title: A Day in the Desert
setting: A busy week and a desert trip

story.text: Khalid is a manager at a bank in Riyadh. He is very **busy**.

From **Sunday** to **Thursday**, Khalid has the same **routine**. He **always** **wakes up** at five **o'clock**. He **prays**, and then he **has a shower**. He **has breakfast** at **half past** six: **eggs**, bread and tea. He **leaves** home at seven o'clock, and he **drives** to work.
Khalid **usually** **gets home** at six in the evening. He is tired. He **often** **watches** **TV**, and he **goes to bed** at ten o'clock.
Khalid's son, Saad, is ten. Saad **studies** in the evening.
"**Dad**, **when** do we **go out**?" says Saad. "We **never** go out!"
"That's true," says Khalid.
Does Khalid **relax**? No, he **doesn't**. He never relaxes!
On Thursday evening, Saad talks to his dad.
"Dad, **tomorrow** is **Friday**. **Let's** go to the **desert**!"
"The desert? **Why not**?" says Khalid. "**Good idea**!"
On Friday, Khalid doesn't wake up **early**. He **gets up** at eight o'clock. In the **morning**, Khalid and Saad **go shopping**. They **buy** water, **fruit**, chicken and bread.

In the afternoon, they drive to the desert. The **sand** is beautiful. Saad helps his dad with the **tent**. Khalid **cooks** the chicken. They **walk** in the sand, and they **stay** in the desert **all day**.
Khalid doesn't watch TV. He doesn't read emails. He relaxes!
"Dad, are you happy?" asks Saad.
"Yes, I'm very happy," says Khalid. "I love the desert!"
"**Next** Friday, let's go to the **beach**!" says Saad.
"**Sure**!" says Khalid.
Now Khalid **sometimes** works late on Thursdays. But on Fridays, he always goes out with Saad.

title: A Jacket for Hail

story.text: Saad lives in Riyadh. His best friend, Majed, lives in Hail. Majed has a new **baby**, and Saad wants to visit them.
Saad goes to the **railway** station.
"Hello. **Can I** have a **return ticket** to Hail, please?"
"Sure. That's ninety riyals. Cash or **card**?" says the man.
"Card, please. Which **platform**?"
"Platform two. Look at the **timetable**. The **train** leaves at half past eight."
"**How long** is the **journey**?"
"Four hours."
The train is **fast** and **comfortable**. A **friendly** **passenger** talks to Saad. He is an **old** man.
"**Why** do you go to Hail?" asks the old man.
"**Because** my friend has a new baby!" says Saad.
"**Wonderful**! But where is your **coat**? Hail is very **cold**!"
"My coat? It's in Riyadh! Riyadh is **hot**."
"Ha! In Hail, it's five **degrees** today."
In Hail, it's cold and **wet**. Saad goes to a **clothes** shop.
"Excuse me. Can I **try on** **that** **jacket**? The **black** one."
"Sure," says the shop worker. "But it's very **expensive**. It's four hundred riyals."
"Oh! And that **grey** jacket?"
"This grey jacket is **cheap**. It's one hundred riyals."
Saad tries on the grey jacket. It's comfortable.
"I love it. Thank you **very much**!"
"**No problem**."
Then Saad **meets** Majed at a **café**.
"Saad! Welcome to Hail!" says Majed. "**Whose** jacket is that?"
"It's my new jacket! I **hate** cold weather!"
Majed laughs.
At Majed's house, Saad looks at the baby. He is in a small **white** **hat**. Saad has a **present** for him: a **red** **jumper**.
"Thank you, Saad!" says Majed. "It's a wonderful present."
"Your baby is **amazing**!" says Saad. "And Hail is amazing, too. But it's very cold!"

title: Where Are the Car Keys?
setting: A new flat and lost car keys

story.text: Majed has a new flat in Riyadh. It's in a **modern** building near a **park**.
**There are** five **rooms**: a **kitchen**, a **bathroom**, a **living room** and two bedrooms. **There is** a small **balcony**, too.
Today, Majed's friend Turki visits him. Turki doesn't drive. He takes the **metro**.
Turki calls Majed. "I'm at the metro station. I **need** **directions**!"

"OK," says Majed. "**Go straight on**. **Turn** **left** at the **roundabout**. **Go past** the **supermarket**. My building is on the **right**, **opposite** the park. It's ten **minutes** **on foot**."
Turki is at the door. "Welcome! Come in!" says Majed.
"This is the living room. There's a big **sofa** and two **armchairs**. There's a **lamp** **next to** the sofa."
"It's very **tidy**!" says Turki.
"And this is the kitchen. There's a new **cooker** and a big **fridge**."
"Your flat is fantastic!" says Turki. "Is there a café near here?"
"Yes, there is. There are **some** nice cafés in the **square**," says Majed. "Let's go. Where are my **car keys**?"
Majed looks at the table. The keys aren't **on** the table. He looks in the **drawer**. They aren't in the drawer.
"Are they **under** the sofa?" asks Turki.
"No, they aren't."
"Are they **behind** the **curtains**?"
"No."
"Are they in your **wardrobe**?"
"No! There aren't **any** keys in the wardrobe."
Turki is thirsty. He opens the fridge. "Majed! Look! There are some car keys in the fridge, **in front of** the milk!"
"Ha! My keys!" says Majed. "My flat is tidy, but I'm not!"
It's a **cool**, **sunny** **winter** day. Majed and Turki go to the **car park**. They drive to a café in the square.

title: Grandfather's Old Photo

story.text: Today is the **first** day of **Eid**. Ali is at his **grandfather**'s house in Riyadh. All the family is there.
Grandfather has a **gift** for Ali. It's an old photo. In the photo, there is a small boy with two **goats**.
"Who is this boy?" asks Ali.
"That boy is me!" says Grandfather. "I **was** eight in this photo."
"Really? When **were** you **born**, Grandfather?"
"I was born in nineteen fifty-two."
"And what's your **date of birth**?"
"I don't know!" says Grandfather. "In my **childhood**, there were no **calendars** in our village. My mother only **said**, 'You were born in **Ramadan**.'"
"Was your village big?" asks Ali.
"No, it **wasn't**. It was small and **simple**. There were **palm trees**, **sheep** and goats. There **weren't** any cars."
"Were there any **toys**?"
"**Only** one! My **toy** was a small camel. My father **made** it from **wood**."
"Was there a school?"
"Yes, there was a small **primary** school. I was the **eldest** son. I **did** a lot of **housework**, too."
"Were you **naughty**?" asks Ali.
Grandfather smiles. "Sometimes!"
"Were there any lamps?"
"No, there weren't. We **had** **candles**. At night, all the family was by the **fire**. My **grandmother** had a lot of **stories**. They were wonderful."
"You **still** have a lot of stories, Grandfather!"
Grandfather laughs. "Last year, I **went** to the village with your **uncle**. We **saw** the old school. And the palm trees are still there!"
"Grandfather, next Eid, let's go to the village together," says Ali.
"Good idea!"
Ali puts the old photo on his desk. It's the best Eid gift.

title: A Weekend in AlUla

story.text: It's Sunday morning. Fahad is at the office. His friend Sami **talks** to him.
"Hi, Fahad! Did you have a good **weekend**?"
"Yes, I did! I **travelled** to AlUla with my brother. We **stayed** there for three days."
"AlUla? Fantastic! **Did you** go **sightseeing**?"
"Yes, we did. On Thursday, we **visited** the **old town**. It's very **ancient**. We **walked** there for two hours."
"Did you visit Hegra, too?"
"We **wanted** to visit Hegra on Friday. But we **didn't** have tickets. The **entrance** was very **crowded**. We were sad."
"Oh no!"
"Then a **guide** **helped** us. He **called** a friend, and we got two tickets for the **bus tour**. We were **lucky**!"
"What did you see?"
"We saw big **rocks**, a green **valley** and an **oasis** with palm trees. The guide talked about the **heritage** of AlUla. I was very **interested**."
"Did you go **hiking**?"
"Yes, we did. On Saturday morning, we walked in the valley for three hours. It was hot, but the view was beautiful."
"Did you take photos?"
"**Lots** of photos! The **view** from the **viewpoint** was amazing."
"And the food?"
"In the evening, we ate **outside**. I had **grilled** **lamb** with rice. My brother had chicken. It was very **tasty**."
"Did you sleep in a hotel?"
"No, we didn't. We stayed in a small **villa** near the old town. It was **relaxing**."
"Great!"
"And you, Sami? What did you do?"
"Me? **Nothing** **special**! I stayed at home. I **watched** TV, and I **cleaned** my car."
"**Not bad**!" says Fahad.
Sami smiles. "I visited AlUla ten years **ago**. Next weekend, I want to go again!"

title: Grandma's Video Call

story.text: Majed's **grandma** is seventy. She **can** cook **really well**. Her kabsa is the best in the family. She can tell wonderful stories, too.
But Grandma **can't** use the Internet. She has a new **tablet**, but it is in her bedroom with no **apps**.
Majed's brother, Hamad, is a student in Canada. Grandma **misses** him a lot.
"Majed, **can you help me**?" asks Grandma. "I want to see Hamad."
"Of course!" says Majed. "We can make a **video call**."
"First, we need the **Wi-Fi**. What's the **password**?"
"I don't know! It's on a paper in the kitchen."
Majed finds the paper. Now the tablet is on the Wi-Fi.
"OK, Grandma. Now we **download** an app. Look. **Click** this **button**."
Grandma **tries**. She clicks very **slowly**.
"Can you do it **fast**?" asks Majed.
"No, I can't!" laughs Grandma. "But I can do it slowly!"
Then the **screen** is black.
"**What's the matter**?" asks Grandma. "Is it **broken**?"
"No, it isn't broken. Don't worry. The **battery** is empty. We need thirty minutes."
In thirty minutes, the battery is full. Grandma **pushes** the green button. And there is Hamad!
"Grandma! Can you hear me?"
"Yes, I can! And I can see you, too!" says Grandma. "Are you OK? Can you cook?"
"I can cook **a little bit**," says Hamad. "But your kabsa is **better**!"
Grandma is very happy.
Now Grandma can make video calls. She can **also** send messages. She calls Hamad every Friday.
"Grandma, you learn fast!" says Majed.
"Yes!" says Grandma. "And I can **type** with one **finger**!"
"Be **careful**, Grandma," says Majed. "Never give your password to people **online**. It isn't **safe**."

title: Too Much Sugar!

story.text: Adel is forty-five. Last month, he **felt** tired every day. He visited his doctor.
"Adel, you eat **too much** sugar and **too many** **sweets**," said the doctor. "Please walk every day, and eat more vegetables."
On Saturday, Adel and his son Hamza go to the supermarket. Hamza takes a **trolley**.
Adel puts **crisps** and chocolate in the trolley.
"Dad! That's too many crisps!" says Hamza.
"OK, OK," says Adel. He puts them back.
They buy some **tomatoes**, **cucumbers**, **onions**, **lettuce** and olive **oil**.
"Are there any **potatoes**?" asks Hamza.
"Yes, there are some here," says a worker.
"A **kilo**, please," says Hamza.
At the **bakery** **counter**, a man smiles at Adel.
"**Would you like** some cake, sir? It's very good today."
Adel looks at the cake. Then he looks at Hamza.
"No, thank you," says Adel. "**I'd like** some brown bread, please."
They go outside to the car. There is a **sign** next to the car: "**No parking**".
A guard comes. "Sir, please read the sign. You can't park here."
"Sorry!" says Adel. "We can go now." He drives to the **car park**.
In the evening, Adel and Hamza walk in the park. They walk four **kilometres**. That's about five thousand **steps**!
Now they walk every evening at **sunset**. Adel **feels** better. He has more **energy**. His **weight** is lower, and his **heart** is **healthier**.
"Dad, you're more **active** now," says Hamza. "And your stomach is **smaller**!"
Adel laughs. "Yes, and I'm happier, too!"
At home, Hamza opens the fridge. "Dad, would you like a chocolate?"
"No, thank you," says Adel. "I'd like an apple!"

title: Warm Blankets
focus: What are you doing right now?

story.text: It's a cold winter night in Riyadh. Yasser is a **volunteer** at a **charity**. Every Thursday, he helps at a **shelter** for **homeless** people. Tonight, he is **helping** with **blankets**.
His phone rings. It's his mother.
"Hello, Yasser. What are you doing **right now**?"
"I'm at the shelter with my friend Ahmed. We're carrying blankets. People **donate** them every winter."
"Are you **wearing** your coat? It's very cold."
"Yes, I'm wearing my coat and my **gloves**."
"And Ahmed?"
"Ahmed is wearing only a thobe. He isn't wearing a jacket. Listen! He's **sneezing** and **coughing**. He **has a cold**."
"Oh no! I'm **worried**," says his mother. "Please tell him to **put on** a **scarf**."
"Ahmed!" says Yasser. "Put on my scarf!"
Ahmed smiles. He is putting on the scarf now. "Thank you, Yasser. Now I'm warm!"
"Mother, an old man is standing at the door. He's **lonely** and cold. Ahmed is giving him a blanket. The man is smiling. He's very **pleased**."
"That's wonderful," says his mother. "Your father pays **zakat** to this charity every year."
"Yes! And now we're helping, too."
"Are you tired?"
"A little. But we're happy. Look! Two children are **waving** at us. They're **holding** their new blankets."
"Good. Please come home at ten o'clock. And Ahmed, **get better** soon!"
At ten o'clock, Yasser and Ahmed are driving home. Ahmed is still sneezing, but he is happy.
He **takes off** the scarf. "Here you are, Yasser. Thank you."
"No, **keep** it," says Yasser. "It's a cold night!"
"Thank you, Yasser. You're a very good friend," says Ahmed.

title: Going to Canada

story.text: Turki is eighteen. He has a **scholarship** to study **abroad**. He is **going to** study **chemistry** at a university in Canada. Tonight, he is going to take an **overnight** **flight**.
Turki's mother and father are at the airport with him. Turki is **nervous**.
"Are you OK, Turki?" asks his father.
"I'm a little nervous. It's a big day."
At **check-in**, a woman smiles at Turki. "Your passport, please. And your **luggage**?"
"This **suitcase**."
"It's thirty-two kilos. That's too heavy. You can only take twenty-three kilos."
Turki opens the suitcase. There are five kilos of dates and three kilos of Saudi coffee!
"Mother!" says Turki.
His mother laughs. "**Never mind**. Take one kilo of dates. Your father can keep the other dates."
Now the suitcase is twenty-three kilos.
"So, what are you going to do in Canada?" asks his father.
"First, I'm going to study English for one **semester**. Then I'm going to **begin** my chemistry **lectures**. I'm going to work hard in the **laboratory**."
"And then?" asks his mother.
"I'm going to **graduate**, and I'm going to come back to Saudi Arabia. My **dream** is to **become** a scientist. I **hope** to work in Riyadh. **One day**, I'm going to have my own laboratory!"
His father smiles. "We're very happy for you."
Then they hear: "Flight 25 to Toronto. **Boarding** now at Gate 15."
"**Have a good trip**, Turki!" says his father. "**Take care**!"
"**Have a safe journey**, my son," says his mother. "Call us every day!"
"I'm going to call you every evening," says Turki. "**See you again soon**!"
"**All the best**!"
Turki waves. He isn't nervous now. He's excited about his **future**.

title: The English Play

story.text: Hamad is a student at a college in Riyadh. He is a little shy. His English is good, but he doesn't speak a lot in class.
One day, his teacher, Mr Adel, has a plan.
"Our English club is going to do a short play at the college **theatre**," says Mr Adel. "It's about an old king and his three sons. Who wants to **join**?"
Hamad thinks about it. Then he **decides** to join. He is going to be the king!
But it isn't easy. Hamad is a new **actor**. He is nervous, and he can't remember his words.
"I can't do it," says Hamad. "My English isn't good enough."
Mr Adel gives him some **advice**. "You **should** practise every day. Read your words slowly. And **believe in yourself**!"
His classmate Fahad helps him, too. Every evening, they **prepare** together **upstairs** in Hamad's room. Hamad reads his words again and again. Slowly, his English **improves**.
On the night of the play, the theatre is full. Hamad's mother and father are there. Hamad is wearing a long, red king's coat and a big, funny **nose**.
The play begins. Hamad's first words are **perfect**. The people laugh at his funny nose.
Then, **during** the play, Hamad forgets his words!
His **face** is red. Everyone is quiet. Then Fahad whispers the words to him. Hamad smiles and continues.
At the end, everyone claps. The play is a big **success**!
"That was **perfect**, Hamad!" says Mr Adel. "I **think** you're a real actor now!"
"I **agree**!" says Fahad.
Hamad laughs. "Thank you for your advice. I think I **prefer** the theatre to the **cinema** now!"
